one_month_reasoning: Inside the Oct 2-31 window: (1) Nebius's leaked GPU/CPU price increases took effect Oct 1 (H100 +17% to $4.50/hr), already partly priced after the Sept 17 +4% move; (2) hyperscaler Q3 reports in the last week of October (Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon), where capex guides matter most for neocloud sentiment; all three of Alphabet/Amazon/Meta raised capex in July and consensus points toward ~$1T in 2027, so a further raise is more likely than a cut, but the stock reacts to tone and any off-balance-sheet/leasing commentary; (3) neocloud credit tone (CoreWeave CDS, Redburn Sell calls of Sept 21). Nebius Q3 results (likely ~Nov 11-12), CoreWeave Q3 and NVIDIA (late Nov) fall just outside. No strong directional edge, so I use a symmetric lognormal around $232.28 with monthly sigma ~28% (106%/3.5 = 30%, trimmed slightly as vol has compressed since the June peak).

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of a capex-driven DCF ($157 at Oct-2027: WACC 12.5%, g 3%, asset turnover 0.48, EBITDA margin 55%, capex $34B in 2027 falling to $15B) and EV/NTM EBITDA ($246: 11x on $9.4B, net debt ~$30B, 320M shares). The DCF is very sensitive: +/-1pt WACC or +/-0.04 turnover moves it by roughly +/-$60-80.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Capex-driven FCFF 2027-2033 + Gordon terminal, valued at Oct-2027. Productive gross PP&E start-2027 $24B + $6B CIP; capex $34B/30/25/20/18/16/15B (2027-33); revenue = 0.48 x prior-year gross PP&E (2027 $14.0B, 2028 $32.9B, 2030 $58.6B); EBITDA margin 50% (2027) then 55%; D&A 13.75% of gross PP&E; tax 25%; WACC 12.5%; terminal g 3% with replacement capex = D&A + g x PP&E. EV $53.3B (PV FCF -$3.0B, PV TV $56.3B) - debt-like $16B + stakes $5.2B = $42.5B / 295M diluted shares = $144 at start-2027, rolled to $157 at Oct-2027. Sensitivity: WACC 12-13% x asset turnover 0.45-0.52 gives $80-$266; bear inputs (turnover 0.40, margin 45%) give negative equity value.

inputs_detail.derivation: Model output, set to sit between Yahoo consensus avg $12.31B (range $8.81-17.99B) and the path to BNP's ~$22B exit-2027 ARR; management says it could sell all 2027 capacity and will add >1GW in 2027.

ARR exit-2026 guide $8B mid vs cumulative ~$30B capex (2026 $20-25B guide + prior years) = ~0.27 on all capex incl. not-yet-productive sites; on productive GPUs, B200 at $5.86-8.09/hr (Silicon Data, Ornn) x 8,760h x ~85% util = ~$44-60k/yr vs ~$65k all-in cost/GPU and H100 still $2.71-3.84/hr 3+ yrs after launch, consistent with 0.45-0.55. Mid-term deals at $20-25M/MW (Nebius) vs CoreWeave $40M/MW short-dated, IREN $20M+/MW 3-yr.

Group adj. EBITDA 41% in Q2-26 and ~40% 2026 guide; AI cloud segment 50% in Q2; CoreWeave runs ~60% adj. EBITDA margin (2025). Scale plus Oct-1 price increases move Nebius toward but not to CoreWeave's level.

2026 guide $20-25B; >1GW new capacity in 2027 at ~$30-35M/MW all-in; 5GW contracted power coming online over 2-3.5 yrs; Redburn estimates ~$250B through 2030 for 5GW (my path is ~$110B through 2030, i.e. I assume only ~2.5-3GW actually built/financed). CoreWeave 2026 capex $35-39B for 1.85GW active is a scale cross-check.
75% GPUs/servers over 6 yrs + 25% buildings/power over 20 yrs; H100 rental prices ($2.50-3.84/hr in Sept 2026) show 3-4 year-old GPUs still earn, supporting ~6-yr lives.
10y UST 5.29% + beta ~1.8 x 5% ERP = ~14.3% cost of equity; ~25% debt at ~7% pre-tax (low-coupon converts, ABS); neocloud credit stress (CoreWeave CDS 855bp) argues against going lower.
Nominal growth near long rates (5.29%) less maturity; AI capex expected near $1T in 2027 supports durable demand but not supernormal terminal growth.

June-30 debt $10.2B less cash $8.04B = $2.2B net debt, plus H2-26 capex (~$22.5B guide mid less $8.1B H1) less H2 EBITDA ~$1B = ~$15.6B; customer prepayments not credited because the matching future revenue is counted in the DCF.
28% of ClickHouse at ~$15B Series D = $4.2B, plus ~$1B judgment for Toloka/Avride/TripleTen.
274.1M outstanding plus convertible/ATM/equity-comp dilution (12.3M shares still available under ATM; $4.3B converts issued Q1-26).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM EBITDA $9.4B (exit-2027 ARR ~$18B x 52%) x 11x = EV $103B; less Oct-2027 net debt ~$30B, plus stakes $5.2B = $78.6B equity / 320M shares = $246.

inputs_detail.derivation: Haircut to BNP's ~$22B; above path implied by 2027 consensus revenue $12.3B; 2026 exit ARR guide $7-9B plus >1GW added in 2027.
Between Nebius AI segment 50% (Q2-26) and CoreWeave ~60%.

CoreWeave EV/LTM EBITDA 14.8x (EV $94B) implies ~11x forward; Nebius has less leverage than CoreWeave (recourse debt $31.4B, CDS 855bp) but Redburn flags greater valuation downside; in a year growth will be slower, so no premium.
Start-2027 debt-like $16B plus ~3/4 of 2027 FCF burn (~-$21B) less assumed ~$8B of new equity (ATM pace of $2.8B/qtr in Q2) = ~$29-30B.
295M diluted + ~$8B equity issued at ~$250 = ~32M shares, rounded down.

bear.story: Funding window narrows (neocloud CDS widen, hyperscaler off-balance-sheet leverage concerns per Redburn), training demand from VC-funded labs cools, GPU rental prices resume falling as Blackwell supply loosens after CoWoS relief; Nebius slows the 5GW build, misses 2026 exit ARR ($7B low end) and 2027 guide disappoints; market values it near invested capital less debt.

base.story: 2026 exit ARR ~$8B, 2027 guide implies $12-14B revenue and ~$18B exit ARR; EBITDA margins drift to low-50s on price increases; capex financed by prepayments, converts, ABS and steady ATM dilution; multiple compresses as growth decelerates, so share price roughly flat to slightly down.

bull.story: Compute stays sold out through 2027 (CoWoS-constrained, hyperscaler capex ~$1T), Blackwell/Rubin pricing holds, Nebius hits BNP-like ~$22B exit-2027 ARR with 55-60% margins and more Meta/Microsoft-scale contracts; stock re-rates toward high-end targets ($399-415).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$115 the market would be pricing equity near invested capital less debt (DCF with asset turnover <=0.45 or WACC >=13.5%), which most likely means a fundamental break: failure to finance the build (equity/convert window shut, prepayments drying up), a major customer (Meta/Microsoft) deferring capacity, or a sharp drop in contracted $/MW pricing, rather than ordinary 100%-vol noise.

key_uncertainties: Durability of GPU rental pricing as Blackwell/Rubin supply loosens (H100 index $2.71-3.84 vs Nebius list $4.50)
Access to ~$100B+ of external financing through 2030 and resulting dilution
Customer concentration (Meta $27B, Microsoft, four >$1B deals) and AI-lab training demand dependent on venture funding
Useful life / depreciation of GPUs, which drives the DCF sign
Hyperscaler 2027 capex path and whether they keep outsourcing to neoclouds
Execution on 5GW contracted power coming online over 2-3.5 years
reasoning: Industry evidence is strong on demand and pricing near term: NVIDIA's AI Clouds/Industrial/Enterprise data-center revenue grew 138% y/y to $40.3B and Q3 is guided to $108B; CoreWeave raised 2026 revenue and capex guides with a $104B (then $129B) backlog; Oracle's RPO hit $664B; hyperscaler 2026 capex >$700B with ~$1T expected in 2027; B200 rental indices are firm ($5.86-8.09/hr) and Nebius is raising list prices from Oct 1. The other side is also industry-wide: CoreWeave CDS at 855bp (~50% implied 5-yr default) in July, Redburn Sell calls ($84 NBIS) arguing training demand only lasts while outside capital does, and H100 prices half their peak. A capex-driven DCF says the equity is worth ~$157 at Oct-2027 on reasonable assumptions (12.5% WACC given 5.29% 10y, 0.48 asset turnover, 55% EBITDA margin), but its range spans negative to >$400 because returns on capital sit near the cost of capital; EV/EBITDA at a CoreWeave-like 11x forward gives $246. Blended fair value ~$201, below the $232 price and the ~$283 consensus target. Scenarios 25/50/25 at $90/$225/$400 (mean ~$235, median ~$225) modeled as a lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.45/0.30/0.30), giving an implied overall dispersion close to the stock's 106% realized vol with a fatter left tail for a financing break. Ladder is roughly at spot at the median, slightly lower, reflecting fair value below price offset by strong industry momentum. Research limited by Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage plan limits (used web sources instead); no option data used.
